comments.body:
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: Spilled request detail is unreachable from the app UI — only the CLI got a viewer**

The PR wires spilling into the app host (`AgentService._persistModelRequest`) and adds a `request blob` section to the **CLI** `/trajectory inspect` (`lib/src/cli/trajectory_tui.dart`), but the app's Request tab got nothing:

- `packages/fa_ui/lib/src/trajectory/trajectory_details_tabs.dart` (`_requestPage`) renders `message.preview` — now always `''` for new sessions — and `message.blocks` — now absent — with no `spillFile` row. `grep spillFile packages/fa_ui/lib flutter_app/lib` finds only the writer side.
- `lib/src/trajectory/trajectory_export.dart:147` renders `'…: ${message.preview…}'` → spilled sessions export as `role · N chars: ` with a dangling colon.

Net effect: for every new app-hosted session the per-message drill-in data still exists on disk (the blob) but is unreachable from the app — a quiet UX regression the CLI half of this PR solved for itself. Please add the same pointer to the app Request tab (a `spillFile` row, or resolve the blob via the exported `TrajectoryRequestBlobStore.readDetail`), or scope this PR to the CLI host until the app viewer exists.

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: "Closes #1745" — but `shell_job_registry` (216 MB of the cited ~875 MB) is untouched**

The ticket (input/ticket.md, Problem Summary) cites two unrotated record kinds in the 1 GB session: `model_request_summary` at 658.75 MB **and `shell_job_registry` at 215.92 MB (2487 records)**. This PR remediates only `model_request_summary`; nothing here touches `shell_job_registry`, so a marathon session still grows unboundedly — just ~4× slower — while the issue auto-closes.

comments.author: unknown
comments.body:
💡 **SUGGESTION: TTL never advances for ended sessions — no boot-time/global sweep**

`enforceBudget()` is only ever called from `_maybeSweep()` inside [write] — i.e. rotation runs only while *that session* keeps receiving requests. Once a session ends, its `.fah/trajectories/<sid>/requests/` dir stops aging: 30-day-old blobs of dead sessions stay forever, and `.fah/trajectories/` accumulates up to 50 MB × N sessions with no reaper. The ticket's letter is per-session ("max 50MB per session"), so this isn't blocking — but the disk-footprint tail the ticket complains about partially survives at the directory level.

Cheap fix: on host boot (or session open), sweep every sibling `requests/` dir under `.fah/trajectories/` against the same TTL — `enforceBudget` already has the age math, it just needs a variant that takes the dir explicitly.

comments.body:
⚠️ **IMPORTANT (re-raised, narrowed after reading the linked issue): "Closes #1745" vs the issue's own triage plan**

The linked issue (github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness#1745, Problem Summary, read this run) cites two unrotated record kinds: `model_request_summary` at **658.75 MB** (1101 records) and `shell_job_registry` at **215.92 MB** (2487 records). This PR ships the second-tier blob offload; the delta-encoding tier is not here. Merging with "Closes #1745" would retire the ticket with the triage's stated core fix unimplemented.
2. The `shell_job_registry` half is already bounded for new runs by #1594's persist-window + dedupe (per the same triage comment) — so no extra work is needed there, but the "quarter of the cited disk growth still open" framing from the earlier review round is resolved by that prior fix.

Neither point blocks: the implementation matches the issue's *Proposed Fix* section verbatim (lightweight metadata in the JSONL + `.fah/trajectories/<sid>/requests/` with TTL/rotation), it reduces the dominant 658.75 MB class, and the measured growth is real. Please just confirm the intent: either keep "Closes #1745" and state that delta-encoding is dropped/deferred deliberately, or drop the closing keyword so the issue stays open for the delta-encoding tier.
